CREATE PROCEDURE [Integration].[GetMovementUpdates]
    @LastCutoff datetime2(7),
    @NewCutoff datetime2(7)
WITH EXECUTE AS OWNER
AS
BEGIN
    SET NOCOUNT ON;
    SET XACT_ABORT ON;

    SELECT sit.[StockItemTransactionID] AS [WWI Stock Item Transaction ID],
           sit.[StockItemID] AS [WWI Stock Item ID],
           sit.[TransactionTypeID] AS [WWI Transaction Type ID],
           sit.[InvoiceID] AS [WWI Invoice ID],
           sit.[SupplierInvoiceNumber] AS [Supplier Invoice Number],
           sit.[CustomerID] AS [WWI Customer ID],
           sit.[PurchaseOrderID] AS [WWI Purchase Order ID],
           CAST(sit.[Quantity] AS int) AS [Quantity],
           sit.[LastEditedWhen] AS [Last Edited When]
    FROM Warehouse.StockItemTransactions sit
    WHERE sit.LastEditedWhen > @LastCutoff
      AND sit.LastEditedWhen <= @NewCutoff
    ORDER BY sit.StockItemTransactionID;
END;

-- initial hand-written draft (same as final except for the Quantity cast)
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION integration.get_movement_updates(
    last_cutoff timestamp, new_cutoff timestamp
)
RETURNS TABLE (
    "WWI Stock Item Transaction ID" integer,
    ...
)
LANGUAGE sql STABLE AS $$
    SELECT ..., sit."Quantity"::integer, ...
    FROM warehouse.stock_item_transactions sit
    WHERE sit."LastEditedWhen" > last_cutoff AND sit."LastEditedWhen" <= new_cutoff
    ORDER BY sit."StockItemTransactionID"
$$;
notes: WITH EXECUTE AS OWNER has no direct PostgreSQL equivalent; omitted in the conversion.
Output columns with spaces (e.g. 'WWI Invoice ID') are double-quoted in PL/pgSQL RETURNS TABLE.
CAST(Quantity AS int) in T-SQL truncates toward zero. PostgreSQL ::int rounds. Correct conversion uses CAST(TRUNC(Quantity) AS integer).
datetime2(7) sub-microsecond values are truncated to microseconds by PostgreSQL timestamp on insert; recorded as load-time findings when observed.

columnMappings.notes: NULL allowed; no explicit NOT NULL constraint
PostgreSQL stores all text as UTF-8 natively; nvarchar -> varchar is lossless for standard Unicode
100ns ticks truncated to microseconds on load into PostgreSQL. Sub-microsecond boundary values can differ between engines before the function even runs. Recorded as load-time finding when observed.
